resources.string: Biceps heads
Front of the right upper arm: two heads join above the elbow.
Long head
The outer head starts at the upper edge of the shoulder socket. Its tendon runs through a groove at the front of the humerus.
Short head
The inner head starts at the coracoid process, a projection of the shoulder blade. It joins the long head toward the elbow.
Distal tendon
This tendon crosses the front of the elbow and attaches to the radial tuberosity near the top of the radius. The biceps bends the elbow and helps turn the palm upward.
Triceps heads
Back of the right upper arm: the deep medial head is visible near the elbow.
Long head
The long head starts just below the shoulder socket on the shoulder blade. It crosses both the shoulder and the elbow.
Lateral head
This superficial head starts high on the back of the humerus and forms the outer part of the triceps.
Medial head
This head starts lower on the back of the humerus. Most of it lies beneath the other two heads, with a portion exposed near the elbow.
Triceps tendon
The tendon attaches at the olecranon, the bony point of the ulna at the back of the elbow. The triceps pulls here to straighten the elbow.
Quadriceps layers
Front of the right thigh, with a separate inset of the deep vastus intermedius.
Rectus femoris
This long, central muscle lies over the vastus intermedius. It starts on the pelvis and helps bend the hip as well as straighten the knee.
Vastus lateralis
This broad muscle starts on the femur and forms the outer part of the quadriceps. It helps straighten the knee.
Vastus medialis
This muscle forms the inner part of the quadriceps. Its lower fibers form a rounded bulge just above the inside of the kneecap.
Vastus intermedius
The inset shows this muscle on the front of the femur with the overlying rectus femoris omitted. Like the other three muscles, it helps straighten the knee.
Quadriceps tendon
The four muscles converge into this tendon above the kneecap. Below the kneecap, the patellar ligament continues to the tibia.
Hamstring muscles
Back of the right thigh: the hamstrings pass to either side of the knee.
Biceps femoris: long head
This outer hamstring head starts at the ischial tuberosity, the sitting bone. Its tendon runs to the head of the fibula on the outside of the knee.
Biceps femoris: short head
The short head starts on the back of the femur, not on the pelvis. It lies partly beneath the long head and joins its tendon near the knee.
Semitendinosus
This muscle shares an attachment at the sitting bone with the long head of the biceps femoris. Its long lower tendon wraps to the inner side of the upper tibia.
Semimembranosus
This broad muscle lies deeper than the semitendinosus. It attaches to the back of the inner tibial condyle near the knee.
